statement: The point $P = (2, 7)$ is reflected across the vertical line $x = 5$. That image is then reflected across the $y$-axis. What are the coordinates of the final image?

choices.misconception: I reflected across x = 5 to get (8, 7) and then forgot to do the second reflection.
I did the first reflection correctly to get (8, 7), but then reflected across the x-axis instead of the y-axis.
I skipped the first reflection and only reflected (2, 7) across the y-axis.
I thought reflecting across x = 5 meant adding 5 to the x-coordinate, which gave (7, 7), and then the y-axis reflection gave (-7, 7).

hints: Reflecting across a vertical line does not change the $y$-coordinate.
$P$ is $3$ units to the left of the line $x = 5$, so its image is $3$ units to the right of that line. Reflecting across the $y$-axis then changes the sign of the $x$-coordinate.
The first image is $(8, 7)$. Reflecting it across the $y$-axis gives the answer.

solutions.reliable: $P$ is $5 - 2 = 3$ units to the left of the line $x = 5$, so its mirror image is $3$ units to the right of the line, at $(8, 7)$. Reflecting across the $y$-axis keeps the $y$-coordinate and changes the sign of the $x$-coordinate, giving $(-8, 7)$.
solutions.elegant: Reflecting $x$ across the line $x = 5$ sends $x$ to $10 - x$, and reflecting across the $y$-axis sends $x$ to $-x$. Together, $x \mapsto -(10 - x) = x - 10$, a slide $10$ units left: $(2, 7) \mapsto (-8, 7)$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
